items.title: A gait foundation model for prediction of multisystem health phenotypes from 3D skeletal motion
items.excerpt: Foundation model trained on 3D skeletal motion from 3,328 adults predicts cardiometabolic, mental-health and frailty diagnoses and clinical characteristics from gait.
items.rationale: Nature Medicine: a walking-gait foundation model reads cardiometabolic, mental-health and frailty diagnoses from 3D motion, opening a low-cost, non-invasive screening signal.

items.title: FDA clears AI-powered intravascular ultrasound imaging platform
items.excerpt: FDA cleared Evident Vascular's Guidance System and peripheral IVUS catheters, which integrate 'purpose-built AI' and NVIDIA-accelerated real-time processing for peripheral vascular procedures; the company plans further AI capabilities.
items.rationale: Regulatory clearance: an AI-integrated IVUS system for peripheral vascular procedures is now cleared for use in the cath/IR lab.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Scribes and Same-Day Note Closure by Patient Language Preference and Interpreter Modality
items.excerpt: Brigham and Women's cross-sectional study of 209,009 primary-care encounters (286 clinicians, 14 clinics): AI scribes raised same-day note closure most for non-English-language-preference visits with a language-concordant clinician (+10.2 points adjusted vs +1.7 for English); interpreter-mediated visits inconclusive. Date per Crossref created.
items.rationale: Equity angle on ambient scribes: across 209k visits the biggest documentation gain came in non-English visits with a language-concordant clinician, while interpreter visits stayed unclear.

items.title: Stroke recovery tracked with wearable device
items.excerpt: NIH-funded UMass team used machine learning on wrist accelerometer data from 61 stroke patients to build a digital arm performance scale (DAPS) that tracked arm recovery as well as clinical tests (Science Translational Medicine).
items.rationale: Rehab monitoring: an ML scale built from a wrist accelerometer tracked stroke patients' arm recovery as well as in-clinic tests, pointing to at-home outcome tracking.

items.title: Deep-learning model predicts mortality from CTA scans
items.excerpt: Cedars-Sinai-led multicenter study (1,674 TAVR-planning patients, 9 sites, JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging) shows a deep-learning model quantifies aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue on CTA in 1.35 min vs 7.2 min for experts; highest fibrotic volume carried 2x mortality risk.
items.rationale: TAVR planning: deep learning quantifies valve fibrosis and calcium on pre-procedure CTA about 5x faster than experts, and the fibrotic burden it measures predicts mortality.
